The Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia recovers water from a spring on Pine Mountain and has a gravity flow system. The spring produces 73,000,000 gallons annually and 40,372,000 galions were sold from July 1, 1985 to June 30, 1986. The budget for the operation of the water and sewerage department FY 86/87 is $120,500.00.

In order to conserve water, the Town of Pine Mountain agrees that: 1, All water will be metered at the spring. Zz. All service connections will be metered. 3. There will be a distribution map and it will be kept updated when replacements, additions and improvements are made. 4, A leak detection program will be instigated with the goal of accounting for 90% of the water produced.

S. A list will be prepared of all major users and the amount of Water they use per day, month or year. 6. A plumbing code ordinance will be established which will include control cf cross-connections and/or inter-connections. The Town of Pine Mountain will comply with the Georgia Water Conservation Act of 1977.

- 7. An ordinance will be passed providing for the priority use of water and the curtailment of water use during emergencies and to assume the authority to impose penalties for non-compliance. ’

- 8. A realistic pricing schedule will be adopted which will increase rates with increased usage. Flat rate pricing will be eliminated.

- 9. Fublic education programs will be instigated and a home water conservation pamphiet will be published.

- 10. Monthly records will be kept to help detect water availability problems.

IMPLEMENTATION The Town of Pine Mountain installed a meter at the spring in early 1986. The churches are the only service connections which are not metered, These connections will be metered by the end of 1986. There is @ distribution map and every effort will be made to keep it updated. The Town enacted a plumbing code nany years age, and there are not any cross-connections or interconnections. The water rates were raised at the beginning of FY 85/86 for the first time since 1962. The water rates were incressed by fifty per cent. However, the rate schedule is a fixed rate schedule. A means of eliminating this fixed rate scheduling will be discussed. A pamphlet with hints For the conservation of water at the home Level is in the process of being published at this time. The flow at the spring house is monitored daily

1: WHEREAS, the Town's water supply is in a critical situation and
2:
it has become necessary for the Mayor and Town council to adopt uniform requirements for the Town's Water Conservation Program

BE IT RESOLVED, and it is hereby resolved that the

Mayor and Town Council adopt the following uniforn requirements for the critical, emergency situation of the Town's water supply and for the health and safety of the Town water users:

- 1. No outside watering of any Rind, including street flushing, public fountains, park irrigation, Watering lawns, gardens shrubbery, etc.

- 2. No commercial and/or public water use such as swimming pools and moter vehicle washing of any kind.

- 3. No commercial and home laundry use except during the hours of 7:00 P M to 7:00 A M.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the enforcement actions of this resolution shall be taken on those users not complying with this water conservation resolution in the following

Manner:

- 1. Any person found to be violating the provisions of this resolution shall be served written notice stating the nature of the violation and shall be issued a warning ticket for this violation.

- 2. On second violation, water service will he terminated and a reconnect fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) will be charged.

- 3. Ali such subsequent violations shall be charged a reconnect fee of two hundred dollars ($200.00) for each violation.

This the thirteenth day of October, 1986

Barbara Bell Ewell
